title: A slicer contract bump on main breaks ork everywhere at once

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Observed 2026-11-12: slicer s453 (relay v12) landed through ork itself; since the slicer command is an editable install of slicer's main checkout, ork immediately refused relays in all 12 projects. ork landed the very slice that broke it, with no warning. Wanted: when a slice under relay changes slicer's RELAY_CONTRACT (`slicer ai relay --json` contract differs between the worktree and main), ork pauses before landing and names the ork version that accepts it.

Evidence (checked 2026-11-18):

- The same risk is live now: slicer s460 sets `RELAY_CONTRACT = 13` on its branch (slicer `6cfb5c18`, `src/slicer/ai.py:259`), while ork accepts only v11 and v12 (`internal/roles/roles.go:113-116`, adj 326). The orchestrator works around it by hand: s460 runs with `--stop-after commit` (run ork-20261118-130321-4cea) and lands only after S432 (accept v13).
- ork's landing has no such check. After the merge-in and re-check it runs `git merge --ff-only` on the main checkout (`internal/engine/land.go:95-97`); the only pre-land refusals are a dirty main (`checkMain`, `internal/engine/landdirty.go:168`) and a red re-check (`landBlocked`, `internal/engine/land.go:263-278`).
- ork cannot learn the landed contract from the installed `slicer`: it imports main's source, so `slicer ai relay` run with `--root WORKTREE` still prints main's version. Printing the worktree's version needs a project-specific command, for example `python3 -m slicer ai relay` with `PYTHONPATH` set to the worktree's `src` (it printed `Contract: relay v13` for the s460 worktree on 2026-11-18).
- The registry already has per-project commands of this kind: `CheckCommand`, `RoundCheckCommand` and the self-host `BuildCommand` (`internal/registry/registry.go:245-256`).
- slicer has no item for this (`slicer --root ../slicer find "contract bump"`: only done items s315, s375, s378, s385, none a consumer guard).

Touches `ork projects set` output and help (internal/cli): it gets a UI pass.

Decided: adj 484 (`land.contract-bump-guard` = probe): a per-project contract probe command, set with `ork projects set NAME --contract-probe CMD`, runs in the worktree before `git merge --ff-only`; the landing pauses on a version ork does not accept.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/registry/registry.go:240-262` (new optional field `ContractProbe`, `json:"contract_probe,omitempty"`)
- `internal/registry/registry_test.go`
- `internal/engine/land.go:90-97` (run the probe in the worktree after the re-check, before `git merge --ff-only`)
- `internal/engine/land_test.go`
- `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:500-510` (`ork projects set --contract-probe CMD`, empty clears)
- `internal/cli/cli_test.go`
- `internal/daemon/handlers.go` (`projects.set` carries the field)
- `docs/state.md` (the registry field)
- `docs/design.md` (landing: the contract probe)
- `docs/guide.md` (setting a probe on the slicer project)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/engine/land_test.go` (harness with a fake probe command routed through clitest):

- `TestLandPausesWhenTheContractProbePrintsAnUnacceptedVersion`: a project with `ContractProbe` set; the probe prints `Contract: relay v13` while the accepted set is {11, 12}. The run pauses in state land before any `merge --ff-only` call, and the reason names v13, the accepted set and "land it after an ork that accepts relay v13". Red today: there is no probe; the run lands.
- `TestLandProceedsWhenTheContractProbePrintsAnAcceptedVersion`: the probe prints `Contract: relay v12`; the run fast-forwards as today. Red today: the field does not exist (compile error).
- `TestLandPausesWhenTheContractProbeFails`: the probe exits 1 or prints no contract line; the run pauses with the probe's error; no fast-forward. Red today: compile error.
- `TestLandWithoutAContractProbeIsUnchanged`: no field set, no probe call, lands as today. Green today; it guards the default.
- `ork retry` on the paused run runs the probe again: covered in `TestLandPausesWhenTheContractProbePrintsAnUnacceptedVersion` by a second probe answer of v12 and a retry that lands.

In `internal/cli/cli_test.go`:

- `TestProjectsSetContractProbe`: `ork projects set demo --contract-probe "CMD"` stores it and the summary line names it; `--contract-probe ""` clears it. Red today: unknown flag.

In `internal/registry/registry_test.go`:

- `TestRegistryRoundTripsContractProbe`: the field is saved and loaded; a registry without it loads with "". Red today: compile error.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests and see each red for the stated reason.
2. Per adj 484 (probe):
3. Registry: optional `ContractProbe` string. `ork projects set NAME --contract-probe CMD` sets it, empty clears it; the daemon's `projects.set` carries it.
4. Landing: when the project has a probe, after the merge-in re-check is green and before `git merge --ff-only`, run the probe in the worktree with the check command's runner and time limit. Read its first output line with `roles.CheckContractLine`. An accepted version proceeds. A refused version, a failed probe or a missing contract line pauses the run in state land (`PendingError`) with a reason that names the version, the accepted set and that the slice can land once ork accepts it; `ork retry` runs the probe again. Never fast-forward on a paused probe.
5. The probe reads only; it is not a fix-round finding and does not count as `LandFixes`.
6. Docs: `docs/state.md` (registry field), `docs/design.md` (landing: the probe, adj record), `docs/guide.md` (how to set a probe on a project whose code is the installed slicer, citing adj 484). Changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S353 --text "..."`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- A project with a contract probe does not land a slice whose probe prints a relay version ork does not accept; the run pauses before the fast-forward and names the version and the accepted set.
- A failed probe or one with no contract line also pauses before the fast-forward.
- A project without a probe lands exactly as before.
- ork projects set can set and clear the probe.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/engine ./internal/cli ./internal/registry -run 'ContractProbe' -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
- `adj lint` exits 0.
- [AFTER LAND] [HUMAN CHECK] the owner sets the probe on the slicer project and runs ork doctor; it shows the contract line as ok.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, message "S353: contract probe pauses a landing that would bump slicer past what ork accepts".
